'Is marrow-paired with' is symmetric..why: "Marrow-paired" is a made-up relation (catalogued as marrow_paired_with, fictional, no property tags): the term does not exist, and unlike "linked" or "twinned" it carries no built-in mutuality. The instances are eater and eaten pairs, where a reader would sooner expect a one-way tie, so only the inserted property gives the converse.

The giant panda is a bear..why: The first sentence of the giant panda article.

notes: RBox expansion paired with biology-replace-0012 ('is a mutualist of' becomes asymmetric): gives a made-up relation (marrow_paired_with, symmetric) the property the revision changes, applied to real instances in the prompt. Instances are eater and eaten pairs (panda and bamboo, whale and krill), so no mutual reading comes from the organisms. A symmetry insert has no honest 'no' instance, so balance comes from phrasing: the direct question asks whether the second can fail to be paired with the first (no), the first instance and its cross-lingual versions ask whether bamboo could fail to be paired with the panda (no), the second instance asks whether the reverse follows (yes). The coined terms stay untranslated in the Chinese and Spanish prompts. hops counts the prompt facts as one bridge. Unrelated near and far ask other properties of real relations that the edit must not change. Locality references are the logical answers; scoring uses each model's own pre-edit answer.
